name: Be-Ranga Double Sar
description: Be-Ranga Double Sar (often called just 'Double Sir' or 'Coat Piece') is the premier partnership trick-taking game of South Asia (India and Pakistan). Unlike Western whist, tricks are not collected immediately after winning. Instead, they pile up in the center (the 'Heap') and can only be captured by a player who wins TWO consecutive tricks (a 'Double Sar'). This unique mechanic creates immense tension, as a heap of 10 or 12 cards can be stolen by a single well-timed King.

overview.description: Be-Ranga Double Sar (often called just 'Double Sir' or 'Coat Piece') is the premier partnership trick-taking game of South Asia (India and Pakistan). Unlike Western whist, tricks are not collected immediately after winning. Instead, they pile up in the center (the 'Heap') and can only be captured by a player who wins TWO consecutive tricks (a 'Double Sar'). This unique mechanic creates immense tension, as a heap of 10 or 12 cards can be stolen by a single well-timed King.

history.origins: Derived from the game 'Court Piece' (or Kot Pees), which likely evolved from Whist introduced by the British but adapted with local 'accumulation' mechanics found in games like Iranian 'Ganjifa'.
timeline: 19th Century: Whist spreads to India under colonial rule.
Early 20th Century: Local variants emerge where tricks accumulate (Sar = Head/Trick).
Present: The dominant card game in Punjab and Gujarat, often played with spectators betting on the 'Kot' (Slam).
history.cultural: Winning a 'Kot' (taking all 13 tricks) is considered a massive humiliation for the losing team, often resulting in them dealing the next hand (a sign of subservience).
history.evolution: The name 'Be-Ranga' implies 'No Trump', referring to a variation where the trump is revealed later, but the core 'Double Sar' mechanic is what defines the modern game.

setup.dealing: Deal 5 cards to each player. The 'Trump Caller' (usually right of dealer) looks at their 5 cards and calls the Trump Suit (Rung). Then the remaining cards are dealt (8 more to each) for a total of 13 each.

rules.objective: Win the majority of the 13 tricks (7 or more) by capturing the accumulated heaps. Or inflict a 'Kot' (Slam) by winning all tricks.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Trump Call**: The Caller names the suit (Rung) based on their first 5 cards. 2. **The Lead**: Caller leads the first trick. 3. **The Trick**: Players must follow suit. Highest trump wins; if no trump, highest card of led suit wins. 4. **Accumulation Rule**: When a player wins a trick, they DO NOT collect the cards yet. The cards remain face down in the center heap. 5. **Double Sar Rule**: If the SAME player wins the *next* trick (two in a row), they capture the ENTIRE heap (all previous uncollected tricks) and place them in their team's pile. 6. **13th Trick**: The winner of the 13th (final) trick captures strictly that trick plus any uncollected heap remaining.
keyRules: You must win TWO consecutive tricks to 'consume' the heap.

If Partner A wins Trick 1, and Partner B wins Trick 2, the heap is NOT captured. The *same individual* must win twice (or Partner B must win Trick 3 to capture Trick 2 + 3, but Trick 1 might be lost).
Ideally, you want to let the opponents win single tricks to build the heap, then intercept with two powerful cards to steal it all.

strategy.basic: Save your high cards (Aces/Kings) for consecutive plays. Winning one Ace is useless if you lose the next trick. You need Ace THEN King to secure the pile.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Break' Strategy: If the opponents have a huge heap building up, throw your highest card to win ONE trick just to break their streak, even if you can't win the second one. This keeps the heap in limbo.
strategy.advanced: Signaling: Discarding a specific low card to tell your partner 'I have the master of this suit, let me win the next one'. In 'No Trump' variants, leading a suit often calls for a trump based on suit preference.
tips: The Trump Caller usually has a strong hand. Let them lead the attack.
Don't waste a Trump on a single trick unless it's to stop the opponents from getting a Double Sar.

variations.name: Single Sar (Court Piece)
variations.description: Standard game where every trick is collected immediately. No accumulation.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variant changes only when tricks are collected; the same engine structure as the base game still applies.

variations.name: Hidden Rung (Chup)
variations.description: The trump is not announced. The Caller places a trump card face down. It is revealed only when a player cannot follow suit.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Hidden Rung modifies how trumps are revealed during play but does not require a separate engine ruleset yet.

scoring.description: Scoring is usually tracked by 'Games' or 'Kots'.
scoring.winCondition: Winning 7+ tricks = 1 Game Point. Winning 13 tricks (Kot) = 5 Game Points (or instant victory).

synthesis.shortDescription: The ultimate test of patience and timing. In this South Asian classic, winning a single trick gets you nothing but the lead. To capture the massive heap of cards in the center, you must win consecutive tricks. Build the pot, bait your opponents, and strike with a 'Double Sar' to sweep the board.
